column1: # Where each Spanish noun's gender in lex-es.tsv was read.
# The tooltip prints a noun's gender beside it, under both forms a row
# weaves. On 2026-10-08 every Spanish noun was read against English
# Wiktionary's Spanish entry, fetched raw, and none was wrong: 169 of the 178
# rows carry the gender of their page's one Spanish noun, and the 9 others
# A Wiktionary page holds every word of one spelling, so a line citing it
# means the gender of this word's own noun there. Five pages hold two: pez,
# fish, is masculine where pez, pitch, is feminine; mañana, morning, is
# feminine where mañana, the near future, is masculine; and cabeza, head,
# mano, hand, and espada, sword, are feminine beside a noun for a person,
# Where Wiktionary gives one word two genders, the seed's is one of them, as
# the Old English and French ledgers have it: soldado, soldier, and médico,
# doctor, are masculine or feminine by the person meant, bebé, baby, is
# given both, and mar, sea, both in one sense. The seed prints all four
# tests/tools/genders.test.ts requires every noun in lex-es.tsv to have a
# line here giving the gender the seed gives, citing the noun's own entry,
# and fails on a line outliving its noun.
# ---- drafted from English Wiktionary via kaikki.org (dump of 2026-11-09), decided_by=wiktionary, status=proposed: woven, labelled, not yet read by a person ----
